title: Middle East conflict to push China needle coke to three-year high
gist: Benchmark expects China needle coke prices to rise sharply in Q4 2026 and peak in Q1 2027 at the highest since early 2023, driven by Middle East conflict lifting crude and slurry oil costs. The text is truncated by a paywall after the oil price detail.

insights.claim: Benchmark forecasts China needle coke prices to rise sharply in Q4 2026 as Middle East conflict pushes crude oil and slurry oil feedstock costs higher.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Feedstock-cost pass-through raises input costs for graphite electrode and battery anode supply chains.
insights.locator: China needle coke prices are expected to rise sharply

insights.claim: Needle coke prices are forecast to peak in Q1 2027 at their highest level since early 2023, before easing as new supply in China comes online.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The price spike is framed as temporary, limited by Chinese capacity additions.
insights.locator: Benchmark forecasts prices to peak in Q1 2027

insights.claim: Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, including key Aramco facilities, raised regional oil supply risk in October 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Attacks on core Saudi assets are a direct supply-risk channel for oil and downstream materials.
insights.locator: Crude oil prices climbed through October

insights.claim: Brent stayed above $100/bbl throughout October, peaking around $117/bbl, then dipped to $90/bbl by 6 November.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sharp retreat to $90 shows the risk premium is volatile and could undercut the bullish needle coke case.
